answer: Lagoon arrival timing. New agents must space their first N actions by a minimum inter-arrival gap drawn from a reference quartz clock; bursts beyond the gap are queued, not rejected. This forces each identity to occupy distinct wall-clock slots, so an attacker must pay real elapsed time per identity rather than parallelizing registrations. To offset queueing, honest agents earn nectar credits proportional to their measured spacing. A thousand-identity flood thus costs roughly a thousand gap intervals of serialized waiting.
